sources.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
sources.locator: Sections 5.1-5.11 (Calculus of Variations), 6.1-6.9 (Lagrangian Dynamics), 7.2-7.9 (symmetries, generalized momentum, generalized energy and the Hamiltonian), 8.1-8.4 (Hamiltonian mechanics and the Legendre transformation), 9.2-9.4 (Hamilton's principle of stationary action), 15.4 (Hamilton-Jacobi theory) with the adjacent headings 15.2-15.3 inspected for scope, and 3.4 (the plane pendulum) and 13.24 (the rolling wheel); read from the local copy fetched by source-fetch-check

contents.name: 5.1 Introduction to the Calculus of Variations
contents.support: The chapter's opening treatment of stationary values of a functional, used here for the example in which a stationary path is not a minimum.

contents.name: 5.2 Euler's Differential Equation
contents.support: The integration-by-parts derivation of Euler's differential equation and its boundary terms.

contents.name: 5.3 Applications of Euler's Equation
contents.reason: Applications to geometry and mechanics outside the variational items of this page; the local arguments are independent and no claim here consumes them.

contents.name: 5.4 Selection of the Independent Variable
contents.reason: Change of the independent variable in variational problems; this page fixes the time variable and does not develop that transformation.

contents.name: 5.5 Functions with Several Independent Variables
contents.reason: Variational problems with several independent variables; the page treats a single time variable and one-dimensional action integrals only.

contents.name: 5.6 Euler's Integral Equation
contents.reason: First integrals of Euler's equation for integrands without explicit dependence on the independent variable; not consumed here.

contents.name: 5.7 Constrained Variational Systems
contents.support: The classification of constraints into algebraic/differential/integral and the statement that the rolling constraint is non-holonomic except for straight vertical rolling, which the planar disk example uses.

contents.name: 5.8 Generalized coordinates in Variational Calculus
contents.support: Coordinate changes in the variational problem, absorbed into the chart-covariance proposition.

contents.name: 5.9 Lagrange multipliers for Holonomic Constraints
contents.support: The multiplier treatment of holonomic constraints and the resulting constraint forces.

contents.name: 5.10 Geodesic
contents.reason: The geodesic variational problem belongs to the differential-geometry material of the library, not to this variations page.

contents.name: 5.11 Variational Approach to Classical Mechanics
contents.support: The passage from the variational principle to the Lagrangian action, absorbed into the definition of the chart.

contents.name: 6.1 Introduction to Lagrangian Dynamics
contents.support: The overview of the three treatments of holonomic constrained motion, used as orientation for the chart definition.

contents.name: 6.2 Newtonian plausibility argument for Lagrangian mechanics
contents.support: The standard Lagrangian L=T-V built from the kinetic energy, absorbed into the mechanical chart Lagrangian.

contents.name: 6.3 Lagrange Equations from d'Alembert's Principle
contents.support: The d'Alembert derivation with generalized coordinates and generalized forces, the reduced form of which is the corollary.

contents.name: 6.4 Lagrange equations from Hamilton's Principle
contents.support: The stationary-action derivation of the Euler-Lagrange equations, absorbed into the first-variation formula.

contents.name: 6.5 Constrained Systems
contents.support: The survey of minimal-coordinate, multiplier and generalized-force treatments, used as orientation for the constrained examples.

contents.name: 6.6 Applying the Euler-Lagrange equations to classical mechanics
contents.reason: Generic solution strategy for mechanics problems; the page proves structural statements rather than carrying out such a strategy.

contents.name: 6.7 Applications to unconstrained systems
contents.reason: Central-force and other unconstrained applications are the subject of other pages of the collection, not of this variations page.

contents.name: 6.8 Applications to systems involving holonomic constraints
contents.support: The disk rolling on an inclined plane with the rolling constraint, the moment of inertia of a uniform disk and the four equivalent derivations.

contents.name: 6.9 Applications involving Non-holonomic Constraints
contents.support: The treatment of non-holonomic constraints and virtual work, against which the d'Alembert/vakonomic counterexample is set.

contents.name: 7.2 Generalized Momentum
contents.support: The generalized momentum p=L_v used in the symmetry identity and charge.

contents.name: 7.3 Invariant Transformations and Noether's Theorem
contents.support: The invariance condition and the associated conserved charge.

contents.name: 7.4 Rotational invariance and conservation of angular momentum
contents.support: The rotational charged used in the translation/rotation/boost corollary.

contents.name: 7.5 Cyclic Coordinates
contents.reason: Cyclic-coordinate reduction and the Routhian are not developed on this page; a separate rigid-body page carries that material.

contents.name: 7.6 Kinetic Energy in Generalized Coordinates
contents.support: The velocity-quadratic kinetic energy in generalized coordinates, absorbed into the mechanical chart Lagrangian.

contents.name: 7.7 Generalized Energy and the Hamiltonian Function
contents.support: Jacobi's generalized energy defined as v L_v - L, used for the reduced energy of the rotating hoop.

contents.name: 7.8 Generalized energy theorem
contents.support: The derivative of the generalized energy and its conservation when the chart has no explicit time dependence.

contents.name: 7.9 Generalized energy and total energy
contents.support: The comparison showing that the generalized energy need not equal the total mechanical energy, exactly the point computed for the rotating hoop.

contents.name: 8.1 Introduction
contents.support: Orientation for the Legendre transformation between the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian descriptions.

contents.name: 8.2 Legendre Transformation between Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics
contents.support: The velocity-momentum transformation and the inversion of the velocity in favour of the momentum.

contents.name: 8.3 Hamilton's Equations of Motion
contents.support: Hamilton's equations obtained from the Legendre transform, absorbed into the branch identities.

contents.name: 8.4 Hamiltonian in Different Coordinate Systems
contents.support: The chart dependence of the Hamiltonian, used for the scope remark on inverse branches.

contents.name: 9.2 Hamilton's Principle of Stationary Action
contents.support: The phase-space stationary action, its endpoint variation p dq - H dt and the resulting Hamilton and Hamilton-Jacobi relations.

contents.name: 9.3 Lagrangian
contents.support: Equivalent Lagrangians and the invariance of the equations of motion under addition of a total time derivative.

contents.name: 9.4 Application of Hamilton's Action Principle to Mechanics
contents.support: The mechanical application of the phase-space principle, absorbed into the phase-action theorem.

contents.name: 15.2 Poisson bracket Representation of Hamiltonian Mechanics
contents.reason: Poisson brackets are not consumed by the variations page; the Hamiltonian formalism there belongs to other pages of the collection.

contents.name: 15.3 Canonical Transformations in Hamiltonian Mechanics
contents.reason: Canonical transformations and generating functions beyond the endpoint action are not developed on this page.

contents.name: 15.4 Hamilton-Jacobi Theory
contents.support: The action functional as generating function, Jacobi's complete integral and the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, the setting of the local action family.

contents.name: 3.4 Geometrical Representations of Dynamical Motion (the plane pendulum)
contents.support: The plane pendulum's energy, equilibria and state-space picture, used for the example's stability discussion.

contents.name: 13.24 The Rolling Wheel
contents.reason: Three-dimensional rolling of a wheel and its tipping stability; this page uses only the planar holonomic special case and does not develop the general non-holonomic wheel.

sources.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), lecture notes
sources.locator: Sections 1.1-1.3 (Newtonian mechanics), 2.1-2.6 (the Lagrangian formalism, constraints, Noether's theorem, applications, small oscillations), 4.1 (Hamilton's equations) and 4.7 (the Hamilton-Jacobi equation); read from the local copy of the PDF served at the cited URL

contents.name: 1.1 Introduction
contents.reason: A course introduction with no mathematical result; nothing in it is used as a premise by any item of this batch.

contents.name: 1.2 Newtonian Mechanics: A Single Particle (1.2.2 Conservation Laws, 1.2.3 Energy, 1.2.4 Examples)
contents.support: Momentum, angular momentum and energy conservation for one particle, and the Galilean group including boosts, absorbed as orientation for the charge corollary.

contents.name: 1.3 Newtonian Mechanics: Many Particles (1.3.1 Momentum Revisited, 1.3.2 Energy Revisited)
contents.support: The many-particle conservation statements, used as orientation for the symmetry charges.

contents.name: 2.1 The Principle of Least Action
contents.support: The first variation, integration by parts and Lagrange's equations, with the explicit remark that the stationary path need not be a minimum.

contents.name: 2.2 Changing Coordinate Systems (2.2.1 Rotating Coordinate Systems, 2.2.2 Hyperbolic Coordinates)
contents.support: The statement and illustration that Lagrange's equations hold in any coordinate system, including time-dependent ones.

contents.name: 2.3 Constraints and Generalised Coordinates (2.3.1 Holonomic Constraints, 2.3.2 Non-Holonomic Constraints, 2.3.3 Summary)
contents.support: The pendulum as a constrained system, holonomic constraints and Lagrange multipliers, and the non-holonomic rolling coin.

contents.name: 2.4 Noether's Theorem and Symmetries (2.4.1 Noether's Theorem)
contents.support: The continuous-symmetry statement and proof of Noether's theorem with the translation and rotation charges.

contents.name: 2.5 Applications (2.5.1 Bead on a Rotating Hoop)
contents.support: Position (2.61), kinetic energy (2.62), potential (2.63), Lagrangian (2.64), effective potential (2.65), equation of motion (2.66) and stationary condition (2.67) for the rotating hoop.

contents.name: 2.6 Small Oscillations and Stability (2.6.1, 2.6.2)
contents.reason: Small oscillations and normal modes are developed on the dynamics page of the collection, not in this variational batch.

contents.name: 4.1 Hamilton's Equations (4.1.1 The Legendre Transform, 4.1.2 Hamilton's Equations, 4.1.3 Examples, 4.1.4 Conservation Laws, 4.1.5 The Principle of Least Action)
contents.support: The Legendre transform and its invertibility, Hamilton's equations, the particle-in-a-potential example and the phase-space variational principle.

contents.name: 4.2 Liouville's Theorem
contents.reason: Liouville measure, the Liouville equation and Poincare recurrence belong to the measure-theoretic recurrence material on other pages.

contents.name: 4.7 The Hamilton-Jacobi Equation (4.7.1 Action and Angles from Hamilton-Jacobi)
contents.support: The action W as a function of the final configuration with dW/dq_final = p_final and the Hamilton-Jacobi equation.

sources.title: J. Cortes, M. de Leon, D. Martin de Diego and S. Martinez, Geometric description of vakonomic and nonholonomic dynamics. Comparison of solutions (SIAM J. Control Optim.), author PDF
sources.locator: Sections 1-2 and 5-6, read from the local copy fetched by source-fetch-check

contents.name: 1. Introduction (vakonomic and nonholonomic dynamics do not coincide in general)
contents.support: The general statement that the two dynamics differ, which the counterexample instantiates with explicit equations.

contents.name: 2. Variational approach to constrained mechanics
contents.support: The variational (vakonomic) formulation with Lagrange multipliers for the constraints, absorbed into the definition of the two laws.

contents.name: 5. Geometric approach to nonholonomic mechanics (Chetaev's principle and equations (5.1))
contents.support: The d'Alembert/Chetaev equations for nonholonomic systems, the formulation to which the non-integrability proposition is addressed.

contents.name: 6. Vakonomic and nonholonomic mechanics: Equivalence of dynamics
contents.support: The algorithm deciding whether a nonholonomic solution is also vakonomic, and the conditions under which equivalence can hold or fail.
